settings.heading: Hear from customers who trust us

settings.question: How do I use it?
settings.answer: Every morning and every evening. Rub [a hazelnut-sized amount] into the skin around each knee for about a minute, until it's absorbed. Then get up and get moving, even if it's just to the kitchen.

settings.question: When will I notice something?
settings.answer: The first time you use it: cool within seconds, then warm, within a minute. The bigger change comes from doing it every day, and that takes a few weeks to become a habit. That's why it's a 90-day course, not a single jar.

settings.question: How is this different from the rubs I already have?
settings.answer: Most rubs are made for bad days. They cool with alcohol that dries the skin, they itch, or they smell like medicine, so they go back in the cabinet once the worst has passed. This one cools through the skin's own cold sensor instead of alcohol, warms after, and looks after your skin with vitamin B3. It's made to be used every day, before the bad days, not after them.

settings.question: Should I rest my knee on a bad day?
settings.answer: Go easier, but don't stop. Use the rub, then take a shorter walk. The aim is to keep moving, not to push through. If your knee is swollen or hot, or you're unsure, check with your doctor first.

settings.question: What's in it?
settings.answer: Menthol, camphor and arnica, the trio in grandmother's rub, plus peppermint, frankincense and tea tree. Vitamin B3 and magnesium chloride for the skin, with shea butter, sunflower oil, aloe vera and vitamin E. A long-lasting cooling agent and a gentle warming agent create the cool-then-warm. No alcohol. [Link: full ingredient list]

settings.question: Is this a subscription?
settings.answer: No. You pay once, and nothing is sent or charged again unless you order again yourself.

settings.question: What if it doesn't work for me?
settings.answer: Then you don't pay for it. Write to us within 90 days and you get every cent back, even if the jars are empty. [Contact: email / phone]

settings.text: Your knees need a few minutes in the morning before they'll bend properly
You take the stairs down more carefully than you'd admit to anyone
Getting up from a low chair or the floor takes both hands
You think twice before a long walk, a trip into town, or a day with the grandchildren

settings.heading: The reason your knees get stiffer every year is not what you were told
settings.text:
You've probably been told it's just your age. Wear and tear, nothing to be done.

That's only half the story.

As we get older, some cells in our knees stop renewing themselves, but they don't clear out the way they should. Scientists call them senescent cells. Most people call them zombie cells. They linger and keep sending out signals that leave the tissue around them stiff and irritated. That's why it gets a little harder every year, even when you haven't done anything differently.

And it isn't only age. In a well-known lab study, human cells kept low on magnesium turned into zombie cells faster. About a quarter of Germans don't get enough magnesium, and some common stomach tablets lower it further; their own leaflets say so.
settings.card_text:
What keeps zombie cells in check is the one thing that feels hardest when your knees are stiff: moving. Cartilage has no blood vessels of its own. It's fed by movement: every step squeezes it like a sponge and lets fresh fluid back in. Research also links regular exercise with fewer zombie cells.

So going easy on your knees feels sensible, but it's exactly what lets the stiffness settle in. That's the rest trap. This rub is built to get you out of it.

settings.heading: What each one does
settings.text:
1. You feel it within a minute. Menthol and peppermint cool the skin within seconds. Then camphor and a gentle warming agent follow with warmth. Cool, then warm, the first time you use it. That minute is your proof: something you can feel, not a promise you have to take on trust.

2. It quiets the noise. Menthol switches on the skin's own cold sensor. Scientists won the 2021 Nobel Prize in Medicine for discovering these sensors, and menthol is how they found the cold one. A strong cool signal takes over the road to your brain, so the ache in your knees quiets down.

3. It gets you moving. This is the one that gets you out of the rest trap. When the first minute of the morning feels good, the first steps are easier to take. Rub it in, and you're up and moving before your knees have time to argue. Do it every day, and moving stops being the hard part.

4. It's gentle enough for every day. Old rubs cooled with alcohol and dried out the skin, and magnesium oil itches. This rub has no alcohol. Vitamin B3 supports the skin's natural barrier, and magnesium salts, the minerals of Dead Sea baths, have been studied for helping dry skin hold moisture. So you can use it every morning and evening without ending up with dry, tight skin.

Four things. One jar. Sixty seconds. Not a rescue for bad days: a ritual for all the others.

settings.label: Stage 1
settings.title: A slow start
settings.text: Your knees need a few minutes in the morning before they'll bend properly. You brush it off. Everyone's a bit stiff at this age.

settings.label: Stage 2
settings.title: You start going easy on them
settings.text: You take the stairs more carefully. The low garden bed can wait. The long walk becomes the short one. It feels sensible, but every day you rest, the stiffness settles in a little deeper.

settings.label: Stage 3
settings.title: Your world gets smaller
settings.text:
You think twice before a trip into town, a day out with the grandchildren, the walk you used to love. You stop planning things. Not because you can't do them, but because you're no longer sure you can.

None of it happens overnight. That's why it's so easy to miss, and why the way out has to be something you do every day.

settings.heading: How the rest trap closes in

settings.eyebrow: The hidden reason nothing has worked
settings.heading: Care isn't something you do once it hurts.
settings.text:
Most of us wait until it's bad. Then out comes the gel from the pharmacy or a painkiller, and once it eases, back in the cabinet they go. In between, we go easy on our knees: skip the garden, take the lift, sit it out.

Every rub you've tried was made for the bad days. Alcohol rubs dry out the skin. Magnesium oil itches. The pharmacy gel smells through your clothes. Painkillers are hard on the stomach. So none of them ever became a habit, and none of them ever got you out of the rest trap.

A garden gate that's opened every day swings easily. Leave it shut all winter and it sticks. Knees are the same.

This rub is made for every day in between.
settings.chart_alt: Illustration, not data: a daily ritual keeps being used, a rescue rub goes back in the cabinet.

settings.title: Proof in the first minute
settings.text:
Rub it in. Within seconds, the cool. Then the warmth, spreading slowly. You'll know on day one that this is different from anything in your cabinet.

Then write down three things you've quietly given up: the long walk, the low garden bed, getting down on the carpet with the grandchildren. Put the note on the fridge, where you'll see it every morning.
settings.points:
Your first cool-then-warm minute
Your three things, on the fridge

settings.title: The minute you look forward to
settings.text:
Every morning and every evening, the same minute: rub, cool, warm, then up and moving. It's the first thing in your day that feels good instead of stiff.

Some mornings will still be hard. That's not the routine failing. That's the morning it matters most.
settings.points:
The first minute of your day stops being the worst one
You don't skip it, because you don't want to

settings.title: The rest trap starts to loosen
settings.text: Now the minute leads somewhere. The walk you'd have skipped. The stairs you'd have avoided. The garden bed you'd have left for "next week." Each one is movement, and movement is what feeds your knees.
settings.points:
You're up and moving before your knees have time to argue
You cross the first thing off your list

settings.title: You stop thinking twice
settings.text:
Researchers at University College London found that a new daily habit takes about 66 days to become automatic, and that missing the odd day doesn't undo it. That's why this is a 90-day course, not one jar.

Somewhere past day 66, it stops being something you do and goes back to being who you are: the one who keeps going.
settings.points:
You say yes before you've checked with your knees
All three are crossed off, and there's a new list on the fridge

settings.heading: Your 90 days out of the rest trap
settings.guarantee_text: 90 days. Every cent back if it hasn't earned its place in your day, even with empty jars.

settings.label: You feel it within a minute
Made for every day, not just bad days
No alcohol to dry out your skin
No medicine smell on your clothes
Vitamin B3 for the skin you rub twice a day

settings.heading: You're not someone who sits things out.
settings.subtitle:
You never have been. You worked hard, you looked after everyone, you kept the garden going and the house running, and you didn't make a fuss about any of it. You're the one who keeps going.

So you're not looking for a miracle. You're looking for something that makes the next step easier, every morning, for long enough to matter.

Winter is when most of us move the least. Dark mornings, cold stairs, every reason to stay in. It's when the rest trap closes fastest.

You can go easy on your knees for one more winter and see where that leaves you in spring. Or you can start your 90 days now. [Seasonal line, update it: Start this week and they finish right around Christmas.]
